Recap and next steps from our side:

1) Quick assumptions I used to build the attached starter model (redwood_prelim_cost_model.xlsx):
   - Avg tokens/interaction: 400 generated tokens + 150 prompt tokens = 550 total tokens
   - Monthly interactions: 70,000
   - Total tokens/mo = 70,000 * 550 = 38.5M tokens

2) Estimated unit costs (starter figures):
   - Hosted baseline (no quantization, standard batch): $160 per 1M tokens
   - Aggressive opt (int8 quant, KV-prefix caching for repeat prompts, batching tuned): $95–110 per 1M tokens depending on latency SLO

3) Feature-level mapping:
   - Conversational triage (higher RLHF/response variability): ~75% of tokens
   - Discharge summary (deterministic, heavy prefix reuse): ~25% of tokens with much better cache hit potential

4) CAC/payback model inputs we need from you to get exact months: CAC per new customer (or per facility), ARPU uplift expected from feature, and expected conversion delta for trial -> paid. Right now, with a $95/1M token baseline and your 38.5M tokens/mo, monthly inference cost ~ $3,657.5. If you need the $/feature metric we can break that down once you confirm active users that touch the feature vs overall patient count.

Attached: redwood_prelim_cost_model.xlsx — it's intentionally simple: toggle token volumes, toggle quantization option, and you get monthly inference run-rate plus $/feature and payback months.

Marissa — quick notes (inline):

> Avg tokens/interaction: 400 generated tokens + 150 prompt tokens = 550 total tokens
- Agree with 550 as a starting point. For triage flows the generated tokens skew higher; plan for 20% upside in peak months.

> Total tokens/mo = 38.5M tokens- Fine. Add scenario rows for 30M / 38.5M / 60M.

> Hosted baseline (no quantization, standard batch): $160 per 1M tokens
- Baseline OK for standard hosted. But if they want a dedicated reservation for predictable latency the unit can drop to $140/1M for committed volumes (12 month commit).

> Aggressive opt (int8 quant, KV-prefix caching for repeat prompts, batching tuned): $95–110 per 1M tokens
- Achievable if they accept slightly higher P99 latency (approx +30–50ms). Also depends on language model size. Recommend quoting two pilot tracks:
  1) Cost-first: int8 + aggressive caching policy — target $95/1M tokens (expected monthly inference $3.66k at 38.5M tokens);
  2) Latency-first: higher perf model, partial quantization — target $130/1M tokens (expected monthly inference $5k at 38.5M tokens).

Caching notes:
- Summary generation likely has 55–65% prefix reuse if they template discharge notes and supply structured data. So revise summary cache to 60% — that lowers effective tokens by ~9–11% overall.

CAC/payback:
- If they target 6 months, we need gross margin on feature > 30% after inference and infra costs. For 9 months, margin can be ~20% and still be acceptable depending on Ops overhead. Rishi, do you want to add product margin targets?

I'll draft a short two-track pilot pricing snippet for Olivia to pick from.

—Karthik
